title: Finite reductions detect integral maps from the smooth orientation line
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the fixed algebraic closure [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. On the small pro-etale sites put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\lim_n(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_W$, $\mathbf1_W=R_W$, and $A_{n,W}=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_W$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Use $D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete constructible category with one common finite Tor interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], its completed pullback and tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and its twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $r_W=\operatorname{red}_W$ for simultaneous derived reduction to actual coefficient towers. Fix a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], put $P=Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and let $G=Rf^!_{\mathcal O_E}$ have its specified adjunction $P\dashv G$ and counit $\epsilon$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $H=R\lim f^!_\bullet r_Y$ have the realized tower adjunction and reduction comparisons of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], and let $\delta:H\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ be the unique counit-preserving comparison [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Set $T=\mathbf1_X(d)[2d]$.

Let $a_\bullet:(A_{n,X}(d)[2d])_n\xrightarrow{\sim}f^!_\bullet r_Y\mathbf1_Y$ be the diagonal tower orientation of [det-sp-tower-gamma]. Let
$$\beta_M:\operatorname{Hom}(M,H\mathbf1_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))}(r_XM,f^!_\bullet r_Y\mathbf1_Y)$$
be the natural Hom bijection of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], oriented as displayed, and $\lambda=\beta_{H\mathbf1_Y}(1)$ its canonical reduction comparison. For $h:T\to G\mathbf1_Y$ define $\rho_n(h)$ to be the ordinary derived reduction of $h$, identifying its target with $f^!_{A_n}A_{n,Y}$ via the reduction comparison for $H$ and $\delta^{-1}$. Then
$$\beta_T(\delta^{-1}h)=\lambda\circ r_X(\delta^{-1}h),\qquad e_n\bigl(\beta_T(\delta^{-1}h)\bigr)=\rho_n(h),$$
where $e_n$ is exact level evaluation [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. The function
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,G\mathbf1_Y)\longrightarrow\prod_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)}(A_{n,X}(d)[2d],f^!_{A_n}A_{n,Y}),\quad h\longmapsto(\rho_n(h))_n$$
is injective. No isomorphism hypothesis is imposed on $h$.

source.place: Clause (1), rank-one tower uniqueness, specialized through the integral Hom bijection to maps from the shifted Tate line

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-integral-orientation-shifted-sheaf-models] for shifted degree-zero presentations r_X(T) ≅ L[2d] and G(r_Y(U)) ≅ W[2d]. Only existence of these models is used; no orientation for a tested map is assumed.

Unfold beta, the fully faithful Hom equivalence and Iso.homCongr. Its value on v is r_X(v) followed by R.rightComparison. Its value on the identity is R.rightComparison, proving naturality and the formula involving targetComparison. Evaluation preserves composition, proving the rho identity.

For shifted single sheaf towers, the composite of the single embedding and common shift is fully faithful. Lift two maps uniquely to sheaf maps x,y. The natural single and shift comparison for each exact evaluation transports equality of their evaluated derived maps to equality of the shifted single maps of e_n(x) and e_n(y). Faithfulness gives e_n(x)=e_n(y). The strict-system equivalence is faithful and a strict morphism is determined by its components; hence x=y and the two derived maps coincide. This is the private Lean helper shifted_single_hom_ext.

Given equal rho families, cancel the finite target comparison isomorphisms using the evaluation identity. Conjugate beta(h delta-inverse) and beta(h-prime delta-inverse) by the shifted sheaf presentations. Their evaluations agree by functoriality, so the preceding helper proves their equality. Cancel the presentations, apply injectivity of beta, and cancel delta inverse to conclude h=h-prime. Neither input map is inverted.
